title: Regionized evidence publish + TTL enforcement and async webhook orchestrator
creator: Priya Nair
description: Summary: Implement a region-aware evidence publishing service and TTL enforcement scheduler that ensures audit artifacts (request/response traces, signed evidence blobs) are stored and exported according to customer residency and retention policies, while exposing a resilient asynchronous webhook API for downstream ingestion and archival partners. This ticket covers the API contract, webhook orchestration logic (batching, backoff, idempotency), per-region residency anchors, and a pluggable TTL eviction pipeline that emits retention events for audit.
background_and_motivation: Customers require cryptographically-signed evidence about inference requests that is anchored to a geo-region for residency compliance, kept for customer-configurable retention windows, and optionally pushed to external evidence stores (S3, partner endpoints). Current evidence pipeline is single-region and synchronous; spikes and partner outages cause failures and data-loss risk. We need an async, durable orchestrator with per-region policies and an eviction/notification flow so Legal/Support/Compliance can automatically get retention and deletion proofs.
acceptance_criteria: API to register evidence publishing subscriptions and per-subscription residency policy (region tag) exists and validates inputs
Webhook dispatcher persists events to an append-only region-anchored queue and retries deliveries with exponential backoff and dead-lettering
Each evidence object is stamped with residency_region and retention_ttl and can be queried or exported per region
TTL scheduler evicts evidence after retention window, emits deletion_proof events signed by our KMS, and surfaces them in the compliance audit stream
Idempotency guaranteed for webhook deliveries (idempotency_key) and idempotent retries for partner endpoints
Operational dashboards for per-region delivery success, DLQ rate, average delivery latency, and TTL eviction lag
api_contract:
Primary endpoints (internal/public-facing as needed):
1) POST /v1/compliance/evidence - Accepts evidence metadata + signed blob location. Returns 202 with receipt_id.
   Required headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>, X-Region: <region>, X-Request-ID: <uuid>
   Body (JSON string example provided below).
2) POST /v1/compliance/subscriptions - Register a webhook/target for evidence export. Fields: target_url, signing_pubkey, region_constraints, max_batch_size, max_batch_interval, retry_policy. Returns subscription_id.
3) POST /v1/compliance/subscriptions/{id}/test - Trigger a test delivery.
4) GET /v1/compliance/evidence/{receipt_id} - Fetch metadata and residency anchor (internal only).
5) GET /v1/compliance/retention-events?region=<r>&from=<ts>&to=<ts> - Stream retention/deletion proofs for compliance auditing.

Contract notes: receipts are canonical and immutable; status transitions: RECEIVED -> PERSISTED -> PUBLISHED -> DELETED. The API accepts region hints but the platform will validate against customer-configured residency mapping and may reject cross-region writes unless allowed.
webhook_payload_examples:
Example: evidence_create event payload:
{
  "event_type": "evidence.create",
  "receipt_id": "rec_9f8e7d6c",
  "customer_id": "acct_2345",
  "residency_region": "eu-west-1",
  "retention_ttl_seconds": 31536000,
  "signed_blob_url": "https://s3.eu-west-1.redwood.example/evidence/rec_9f8e7d6c.sig",
  "created_at": "2025-11-12T15:04:05Z",
  "metadata": { "model": "redwood/gpt-3x", "input_hash": "sha256:abcd..." }
}
Signed header: X-Redwood-Signature: sha256=<signature>
Example: deletion_proof payload:
{
  "event_type": "evidence.deletion_proof",
  "receipt_id": "rec_9f8e7d6c",
  "deleted_at": "2025-11-20T06:00:00Z",
  "retention_policy": "customer:acct_2345:ttl=31536000",
  "kms_signature": "base64sig=="
}
delivery_semantics_and_retries:
- Persistence first: All incoming evidence is written to an append-only regional queue (region-determined by X-Region header / customer mapping).
- Delivery retries: exponential backoff with jitter (initial 2s, max 1hr), 10 attempts before DLQ.
- DLQ flow: emit dlq.unprocessed event to internal compliance stream, and surface subscription to ops paging if >5 DLQ items in 1h.
- Idempotency: X-Idempotency-Key header required for subscribers to detect duplicates; the dispatcher will include delivery_attempt and delivery_id fields.
- Signing: webhooks must be signed with HMAC-SHA256 using per-subscription secret; platform will also attach a signed KMS envelope for deletion_proof events.
storage_and_residency_model:
- Evidence metadata stored in regional Postgres clusters with cross-region replication only for control-plane metadata (no evidence blobs).
- Blobs (signed artifacts) stored in region-specific object stores (S3 buckets or on-prem equivalents).
- Residency anchor record contains physical bucket ARN, region tag, and cryptographic hash linking metadata and blob.
- Read path: evidence fetches are served from region-local storage; cross-region export requires explicit customer allowlist.
ttl_scheduler_design:
- A distributed scheduler (leader-elected per-region) scans for records with retention_ttl_seconds <= now and enqueues deletion jobs.
- Deletion job atomically removes blob (or marks for deletion if HSM/air-gapped) and emits deletion_proof event signed by KMS.
- For on-prem customers with air-gapped stores, scheduler emits an instruction to customer-managed agent to perform deletion; agent must report back signed attestations.
monitoring_and_alerting_playbook:
- Alert: DLQ > 50 items in 15m for any region -> P1 ops paging.
- Alert: eviction_lag_seconds > 1 hour beyond SLA -> P2 notification to compliance eng.
- Runbook: For partner outages, escalate to subscription owner, mark subscription paused, switch to partner-s3 fallback (if configured) and continue publishing to internal archive.
backward_compatibility_and_migration:
- Accept prior evidence API payloads (legacy fields) and map to new canonical schema in ingestion layer.
- Add feature flag to opt-in to per-region firm enforcement; default to permissive for legacy customers.
- Migration job: rehydrate older receipts with region tag based on customer config and reconcile retention windows before enabling hard deletion.
security_notes:
- All deletion_proof events must be signed by our KMS key and include key_id metadata.
- Webhook subscription secrets are stored in vault with access control restricted to compliance-orchestrator service account.
- Security review to validate that signed proofs cannot be replayed or forged; rotate signing keys quarterly and support key_id in payloads.
testing_and_validation_plan: Unit tests for persistence, region validation, and TTL calculation
Integration test: register subscription -> ingest evidence in region -> verify delivery to test webhook endpoint -> assert idempotency behavior
Chaos test: simulate partner endpoint outage and validate DLQ and fallback behaviors
E2E privacy test with air-gapped customer: verify agent-driven deletion attestation flow
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal only): deploy orchestrator in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 behind feature-flag, enable test subscriptions for internal tenants
Phase 2 (beta): invite 3 customers with known residency requirements to test subscription flows and deletion proofs
Phase 3: enable enforcement for all new subscriptions, run migration for legacy customers over 2 weeks
Phase 4: GA and add to console subscription UI and retention controls

blockers: KMS cross-region signing latency: need key proxies or regional keys (security decision pending)
On-prem agent protocol: need product signoff on minimal attestation fields
Customer residency mapping API not yet finalized (dependency on product)
decisions_made: Use per-region object stores for blobs; no cross-region replication of blobs by default
Emit signed deletion_proof events rather than returning synchronous deletion acknowledgements
Use append-only regional queues for durability and ordering guarantees
